title: Forces, density and pressure

parts.text:
13 A rigid rod XY has negligible mass and length 75 cm. The rod is suspended from a fixed point P
by a string attached to end X. An object of mass 11 kg is suspended by a string that is attached to
the rod at a distance of 25 cm from end X, as shown.
P
75 cm
X
Y
25 cm
11 kg
Which vertically upward force acting on end Y of the rod would hold the rod horizontally in
equilibrium?
A
3.7 N
B
33 N
C
36 N
D
320 N

hints: Notice the pivot for moments can be taken at end X where the suspension string acts, so the 11 kg weight acts 25 cm from X and the unknown force at Y acts 75 cm from X.
Recall that for no rotation the sum of clockwise moments about X must equal the sum of anticlockwise moments, with weight $W = mg$ using $m = 11 \text{ kg}$.
Set up $F_Y \times 75 \text{ cm} = 11g \times 25 \text{ cm}$ and notice the distances give a simple 25/75 ratio before calculating in $\text{N}$.
walkthrough: Take moments about end X to eliminate the unknown tension at X. The rod has negligible mass, so only two forces create moments about X.
Calculate the downward weight of the object: $W = mg = 11 \times 9.81 \approx 108 \text{ N}$ acting $25 \text{ cm}$ from X.
Let the upward force at Y be $F$. It acts $75 \text{ cm}$ from X in the opposite rotational sense to the weight.
For horizontal equilibrium, resultant moment about X is zero: $F \times 75 = W \times 25$. Hence $F = W \times 25/75 = W/3$.
Substitute $W$: $F \approx 108/3 = 36 \text{ N}$ upward. This is option C.

A.explanation: This divides the 11 kg mass by 3 but omits weight, so it has units of kg not force and is too small by factor $g$.

B.explanation: This is close because it uses the correct moment ratio of 1/3, but with $g$ approximated as $9.0$ instead of $9.81$, giving about $33 \text{ N}$.

C.explanation: Taking moments about X gives $F \times 75 = 11g \times 25$, so $F$ is one-third of the $11 \text{ kg}$ weight, about $36 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: This multiplies the weight by 3 instead of dividing by 3, equivalent to swapping the 25 cm and 75 cm moment arms.
